questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, what happens?

options.text: The motorcycle jerks and the rear tire may skid.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine makes a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle jerks and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, the motorcycle will jerk and the rear tire may skid.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Get closer to the vehicle ahead.
Stay farther behind the vehicle ahead.
Do not use your high beam headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distance in the dark. Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles when riding at night. Use your high beam anytime you are not meeting or following another vehicle.

questions.question: What protects a rider the best?
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face if you crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield or eyeglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, what is the best way?

options.text: One rider passes completely before the next rider starts to pass.
Multiple riders pass the vehicle at the same time.
The last rider waves to signal no more motorcycles are coming.
Riders pass in a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: One rider passes completely before the next rider starts to pass.
questions.explanation: Group riders should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing and return to formation before the next rider starts to pass.

questions.question: How do you maintain control while turning?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.

questions.explanation: Look ahead through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before turning and lean the motorcycle in the correct direction.

questions.question: What should you do if you are riding next to another vehicle?

options.text: Stay next to it until the next exit.
Let the other driver handle it.

questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in its blind spot. The vehicle may also block your escape route. Speed up or drop back to move away from it.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you need to brake, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the brake on the good tire.
Use only the brake on the flat tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the brake on the good tire.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, gradually use only the brake on the good tire.

questions.question: How much stopping power does the front brake provide?
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides about 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What should a face shield NOT be?
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be scratch-free, see-through on the sides, and fasten securely. It should allow air to pass through so it does not fog up and make it hard to see.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog is chasing you?

options.text: Stop and wait for it to lose interest.
Slow down, then speed up quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, then speed up quickly.
questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. If chased by a dog, downshift and approach it slowly. Then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.question: A person is legally intoxicated with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher.
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a BAC of 0.08 percent means a person is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to drive while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: A motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Can tip over if turning too fast.
Is designed to take corners at any speed.
Should not be used for loading items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can tip over if turning too fast.
questions.explanation: Even with three wheels, a motorcycle with a sidecar can tip over if you turn too sharply or go too fast around a corner.

questions.question: When riding near stopped or slow cars, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Pull over and wait for traffic to move.
Ride on the shoulder to pass quickly.
Weave between the cars to pass quickly.

questions.explanation: Weaving between parked or slow cars is dangerous. Car doors may open or cars may pull into traffic without warning. You won't have space to escape. Never ride on the road shoulder because other drivers won't expect you there.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Practice riding on a quiet road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on a quiet road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger or heavy load in traffic, practice on a quiet road first. This will help you get used to how your motorcycle handles with the extra weight.

questions.question: A good lane position should do everything except:

options.text: Help you see others and be seen.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It helps you avoid hazards and wind blasts. It prevents other riders from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed. Lane position cannot help you avoid traffic signals.

questions.question: To be more visible, you should:

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright and reflective clothing, keep your headlight on at all times, and change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: A group of riders should merge onto a highway in:
questions.explanation: While a staggered line works best under normal conditions, use a single-file line when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time with firm pressure. Don't panic if the brakes lock.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Either the front or rear brake, but not both.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Ride in the far left portion of the lane.
Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When riding behind a car, position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Riding in the center of the lane usually puts you in the middle of their mirror, where the driver is most likely to notice you.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT protective clothing for riders?
questions.explanation: A leather jacket, long denim pants, and full-fingered gloves all protect riders in a fall. Riders should wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or heavy shoes that support the ankles.

questions.question: Which is a problem with a helmet?

options.text: It does not meet U.S. DOT standards.
It was worn during a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: It was worn during a crash.
questions.explanation: A good helmet meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly, and has no defects. A helmet that was worn in a crash should be replaced, even if it looks fine.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards or conditions.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes a vehicle on a two-lane road, how should they pass?

options.text: In a staggered formation with several riders passing at the same time

questions.explanation: Riders should pass one at a time on a two-lane road. Each rider must finish passing before the next rider begins.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you assume?

options.text: Other drivers can see you as easily as they see other vehicles
You do not need to make yourself visible to other drivers

questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer lights than other vehicles, so they are hard to see. For safety, ride defensively and assume other drivers do not see you.
